openai/gpt-5.6-sol.title: Clock reuses one timestamp for eight reads, allowing expired entries to be returned in violation of A2.
Adding ttl_ms to the current time can overflow, panic, or produce an already-expired deadline.
Replacing an existing key in a full cache skips the eviction that A1 requires before every full-cache insertion.
Eviction pops the back of the queue and therefore removes the most recently used entry instead of the least recently used entry.
Key lookup records a hit before checking expiry, so expired entries increment hits instead of misses.
Handle lookup never compares generations, so a handle issued before clear can resolve a reinserted value.
Every eviction appends a tombstone without any normal-operation drain, allowing bookkeeping memory to grow without bound.
hit_rate can overflow when summing the public hit and miss counters, causing a panic or an incorrect rate.

fireworks-ai/accounts/fireworks/models/g.title: evict_one pops the back of the recency queue (MRU) instead of the front (LRU), evicting the most recently used entry in direct violation of A3.
get calls record_hit before the expiry check, so an expired entry that returns None is counted as a hit instead of a miss, violating A5.
get_by_handle never compares handle.generation to the entry's generation, so a handle issued before clear still resolves after the same key is reinserted, violating A4.
now_ms reuses a cached timestamp for up to 8 reads before resampling, violating A2's requirement that every expiry decision reads time fresh and never reuses a value from an earlier operation.
tombstones is pushed on every eviction but compact_tombstones is never called during normal operation, so the auxiliary structure grows without bound, violating A6.
expires_at_ms is computed with unchecked u64 addition (now_ms + ttl_ms) that wraps in release mode, making a large ttl_ms produce an immediately-expired entry.
